results.name: Automated Subversion and Attempted Takeover of AI Pentesting Harnesses
results.description: Unprotected Cairn AI intrusion harnesses are being systematically compromised by unknown actors through automated campaigns that began around October 20, 2026. Attackers insert malicious tasks that manipulate agents to compromise the host systems, involving profiling installations, stealing secrets including AI model API keys, downloading Poseidon malware, and installing unauthorized SSH keys. Two distinct threat clusters, designated AIA0009 and AIA0010, conduct synchronized waves of attacks across multiple panels. AIA0009 focuses on persistence and malware deployment, while AIA0010 emphasizes exploration and credential extraction. The campaigns appear highly automated and possibly agentic, utilizing AI to attack AI operations. Activities include container escape attempts, reconnaissance of host environments, and deployment of Poseidon RAT configured with Bunny.net CDN command and control infrastructure.

results.name: Camera Management Software Compromise Leads to Malware Deployment
results.description: Attackers compromised camera management software (CMS.exe) to gain initial access to multiple organizational environments. Following compromise, adversaries deployed rs.win32.exe into user AppData directories and leveraged DLL sideloading by placing the legitimate Windows binary WpcMon.exe alongside malicious DLLs (IPHLPAPI.DLL and samcli.dll) in non-standard locations. These modified DLLs, based on zlib compression libraries, incorporated beaconing functionality to communicate with a command-and-control server at 144.172.116.37. Persistence was established through Run Key registry modifications. The camera management software, potentially linked to 3R Global and kvision.ai, lacked adequate security controls and logging capabilities. Organizations should treat camera systems and their management platforms as critical components of the enterprise attack surface, implementing proper access controls, monitoring unusual process chains, and restricting executable execution in user-writable paths.

results.name: Signed by Microsoft and Mozilla: a Brazilian kit that hands your logged-in browser to an operator
results.description: HardwareInfo.msi is a Windows installer that quietly sets up a browser-hijacking kit aimed at Brazilian users. It does not install a program you would recognise. Instead, it drops a private copy of Python plus a renamed genuine Windows program, which is used to load a fake system DLL signed by a Dutch company. The real logic lives in a compiled Python module, also signed. That module closes your browsers, plants a malicious extension in Chrome, Edge and Firefox, and copies your saved passwords and cookies. It also prepares a hidden copy of Chrome that an operator can drive remotely while logged in as you.

results.name: PHP2Shell: Exploitation Attempts and Remediation Trends
results.description: Wiz Research has been monitoring exploitation attempts targeting two critical PHP vulnerabilities since their public disclosure on October 21, 2026. While no successful attacks have been observed in their telemetry, some private exploits have been shared that work against various targets. Telemetry shows a 67% decrease in exposed vulnerable machines and a 47.9% reduction in significantly affected organizations within one week. Observed exploitation attempts include tools using the PHP2Shell mechanism matching public proof-of-concepts, though none completed the full exploit chain. Challenges preventing successful exploitation include request-size limits, memory exhaustion failures, and difficulties with worker pinning across different PHP configurations. Additionally, some tools branded as PHP2Shell exploits actually relied on unrelated session poisoning techniques requiring separate local file inclusion vulnerabilities. Despite limited success to date, PHP2Shell remains a significant risk requiring immedia...

results.name: SYS010 Malware Targets Meta Business Accounts
results.description: A sophisticated malvertising operation designated SYS010 leverages paid Meta advertisements promoting free animated wallpaper applications to compromise Meta Business accounts. The campaign distributes malicious browser extensions through fraudulent websites impersonating legitimate software like Wallpaper Engine. These extensions steal browser cookies, harvest Meta Business data, access email accounts, and delete security alerts. The operation employs a modular architecture with PHP-based loaders, SourceGuardian-encoded scripts, and browser extensions for Chrome, Edge, and Firefox. Attackers maintain persistence through scheduled tasks and utilize dynamic C2 infrastructure with authentication mechanisms. The campaign demonstrates significant evolution from its SYS01 predecessor, featuring improved operational security, server-side decision making, and enhanced email manipulation capabilities targeting Gmail and Outlook to intercept and delete authentication codes and security notifications.

results.name: US hospital credentials taken, a US manufacturer's cloud accessed, law firms and federal agencies next
results.description: Researchers discovered three exposed open directories containing files from an active intrusion crew targeting US organizations. Confirmed compromises include a large US hospital system whose staff credentials, 8,460-address directory, and VPN session logs were obtained, plus a US manufacturer whose Azure cloud storage was enumerated with a live SAS token capturing 155,568 object names. The operators deployed a sophisticated toolkit including a malicious JDBC driver chaining to Apollo-derived Windows payloads and Poseidon Linux implants, while targeting hundreds of US law firms and federal agencies including HRSA, SBA, NEA, NSF, and NCUA through VPN and Citrix gateway reconnaissance. Outside the US, confirmed breaches include a Bangladeshi university with 35,601 Kerberos key records exported and a Swiss tax office with domain databases staged. results.name: Inside ICMacOS: From an Infostealer to a Persistent RAT
results.description: ICMacOS (Icarus macOS) is a newly identified macOS Malware-as-a-Service stealer actively marketed since September 2026 by the Russian-speaking actor GlowComa on underground forums. The malware targets macOS systems running Sierra through current versions on both Intel and Apple Silicon architectures. Initially designed as a credential stealer, it rapidly evolved into a persistent remote access trojan with WebSocket-based command-and-control capabilities. The infection chain uses ClickFix social engineering to deliver dropper scripts that harvest administrator passwords through fake system dialogs before deploying the primary payload. Version 1 focuses on stealing browser credentials, cryptocurrency wallets, developer secrets, messaging data, and password managers. Version 2 introduces full RAT functionality with LaunchAgent persistence and interactive shell access while expanding data collection to include Steam accounts, Outlook data, and additional password managers.

results.name: PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618/9) Havoc: UNC actors leveraging Public Exploit Code Against Public, Business And Educational Infrastructure
results.description: Two critical use-after-free vulnerabilities in the PHP engine, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, rated CVSS 9.2, affect the session.upload_progress feature. These flaws trigger during multipart request parsing before application code executes, bypassing WAFs and enabling unauthenticated remote code execution. Within 48 hours of the October 21, 2026 patch release, exploit code spread rapidly across GitHub. Diverse UNC actors deployed automated scanning and exploitation tools targeting over 70% of internet-facing PHP infrastructure running unpatched versions (prior to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35). Observed campaigns include mass exploitation scripts, Mirai botnet C2 infrastructure, session poisoning chains via WordPress LFI vulnerabilities, and automated reconnaissance using proxy pools. Honeynet telemetry captured active exploitation from multiple IP addresses, demonstrating weaponization across public, educational, and business sectors globally.

results.name: How VBScript Malware Evades Detection Using Trusted Tools Copy
results.description: Three malware campaigns using VBScript have been identified targeting victims primarily in Brazil and Portugal through phishing attacks. The campaigns deliver Overlord RAT, Lampion trojan, and an unknown RAT using fake legal notices, financial documents, and invoice pages. Attackers employ multi-stage execution chains involving obfuscated VBScript, batch files, and DLL side-loading with legitimate Windows components like VMware network libraries and VLC player. The malware establishes persistence through scheduled tasks and registry modifications while attempting to evade detection by adding Defender exclusions and checking for virtualized environments. Infrastructure analysis reveals Brazilian-based command and control servers, with payloads delivered through cloud services including Dropbox, Google Cloud Storage, and AWS S3. results.name: ROMULUS ClickFix to LegionLoader and Warden Stealer: Breaking Down a Multi-Stage Malware Intrusion
results.description: In November 2024, a multi-stage intrusion was identified involving ROMULUS, a ClickFix delivery system. The attack chain begins with a ClickFix lure that tricks victims into executing a malicious MSI file through a clipboard-copied command. The MSI decrypts and executes multiple embedded stages using VBScript, PowerShell, and C# loaders. A sophisticated work object callback mechanism executes shellcode that performs extensive anti-analysis checks, including querying IPInfo's API for hosting-affiliated IP addresses and detecting virtual machine display adapters. The shellcode reflectively loads LegionLoader, which registers with its command and control server using RC4-encrypted communications and CRC32 hashing for victim identification. LegionLoader then downloads and injects Warden Loader via process hollowing into ilasm.exe, ultimately deploying Warden Stealer.
